"For instance, in our experiment we showed that when looking at images of objects with only one object per second, such as the moon or stars, the light-absorbing surfaces show a distinct light-absorbing surface."
The researchers were able to calculate the dimness of each object by comparing its brightness against the brightness of other objects in the same location. They also found that the light-absorbing surfaces were very similar to those seen in normal objects.

The boiling point of water at sea level is about 0.576°F (1.34°C) above normal for a saturated solution and the freezing point of water is 24 °C (18 °F).
The temperature at which a saturated solution melts depends on how much pressure there is with the liquid. As you increase the pressure, the resulting liquid expands more rapidly and becomes colder and denser as it escapes from the liquid. If the temperature drops below freezing, the molecules in the liquid become less dense and the molecules will evaporate faster. If they lose their ability to hold their position, the molecules will stay frozen until they reach the melting point.
Is the boiling point of water stable or unstable?
